content.text:
I like this: it's a single rule that covers all three styles, and it's better than my closing-only version, which was a special case of it. I'd change one word, though, because "next" has a catch.

## The catch in "next"
Taken literally, the next work commit after an agent commit may belong to a different agent commit. Suppose rungs A and B name agent `@` X, and X gets committed. The next work commit, C, now names the new `@`, Y:

```
C:  ochid: Y    ocid: <SHA of X>
```

The two trailers would point at different agent commits on one commit, so a reader couldn't tell what `ocid` means without knowing the history.

The closing shows the same catch from the other side. It's made before the agent commit, so the agent commit's literal "next" work commit would be the next cycle's opening.

## The rule I'd use instead
**`ocid`, when present, is the SHA of the agent commit that the same commit's `ochid` names. Exactly one work commit carries it: the last one that agent commit names.**

| Style | Who carries `ocid` | Rewrites |
|---|---|---|
| 1:1 pairs | every commit, since the agent commit is made first | none |
| N:1 local cycle | the closing, `xxxx` until the seal | one, the closing |
| Mixed | the last commit of each group | at most one per group still using `xxxx` |
| Last cycle's landed commits | all 12 | none; they still satisfy the first half of the rule, so history stays valid if a validator allows the extra copies |

## What this gets us
- **Rungs never carry `xxxx`:** a rung simply has no `ocid` line, so the placeholder exists only on a closing, and the guard only has to look there.
- **One code path:** "the agent commit names every unsealed work commit that names it" covers both the pair and the seal, with a pair just being N = 1.
- **It survives reshaping:** the rule depends on what the trailers say, not on position, so a reorder doesn't break it. Dropping the carrying commit only loses a link, because `ochid` still resolves on the others.
- **Rungs keep their SHAs:** tested and shared rungs match what's released, with only the closing changing at the seal.

## What it costs
- **Reader links:** a GitHub reader on a rung has no clickable link to the agent commit and goes through the closing. `lookup` and the planned index use `ochid`, so they aren't affected.
- **Stacks:** two closings sharing one agent `@` would both hold `xxxx`, and filling the lower one changes the upper one's `pcid`. That's a small cascade, only in stacks. Making only the top closing carry it avoids this.
- **Code that assumes every commit has one:** `trailers --update` and the commit and land stamping need changing. `validate-desc` also needs checking, because it may treat a missing `ocid` as a fault. I haven't read that code for this yet.

## The zero-rewrite option
Applying your rule literally has one real attraction: the next cycle's opening carries the previous agent commit's SHA, so **no work commit is ever rewritten**. Every tested SHA would equal the released SHA, and the closing would stay exactly as tested.

I wouldn't choose it. The main reason is that `main`'s landmark commit would have no link to its own conversation, and that link would sit on the next cycle's opening, which might not exist for weeks. It would also need `ocid` to mean "the previous agent commit", which brings back the two-agent-commits problem above. One rewrite of a commit that nothing else is built on seems the better price.

**Your decision:** do you want the "same commit's `ochid`" rule with one rewrite at the seal, or the literal next commit with none? I recommend the first.

The plain version: your rule works once "next" becomes "the last work commit that agent commit names". Pairs get `ocid` on every commit, a local cycle gets it only on the closing, and mixed cycles get it on the last commit of each group. Only a closing ever waits on `xxxx`, so at most that one commit is rewritten.

content.text:
Yes, it's general. The link is a many-to-many relation, and 1:1, N:1, 1:M and N:M are all just shapes of it. It holds with one change to my wording and one limit, which comes from publishing, not the model.

## The rule, generalized
- **`ochid`:** a work commit has one line per agent commit it relates to, and an agent commit has one line per work commit it relates to.
- **`ocid`:** every `ocid` on a commit is the SHA of an agent commit that the same commit's `ochid` lines name.
- **Carrier:** each agent commit's SHA is carried by exactly one work commit, normally the last one it names.

`ocid` lines have to be matched to `ochid` lines by resolving the SHA to its change id, not by line order, because a commit can name two agent commits and carry the SHA of only one. A closing can then correctly hold a real `ocid` for an earlier agent commit and `xxxx` for the current `@`.

## The limit
Adding an agent commit after a work commit exists means changing that commit's description. That's fine while it's local, or on a topic bookmark you're willing to force-push. Once it's on the release line, the link can only be one-way: the agent commit names the work commit, but the work commit can't name it back. So the validators can't require links to be mutual, and only the index would see the reverse direction.

## What this changes
- **My objection to "next" mostly goes away:** with multiple `ochid` lines allowed, the next commit can name both agent commits and carry the earlier SHA without contradiction. The earlier agent commit won't name it back, so that's a one-way link. I'd keep "last one named" as the normal case and use "next commit" as the fallback when the last one is already on the release line.
- **A guard I proposed goes away:** I said committing the agent `@` mid-cycle should refuse or warn. Under this model it's legal; it just splits the relation into another group. The real problem becomes **Land** assuming a single `@`, which it would have to stop doing.
- **The durability gap can close:** you could commit and push the agent repo mid-cycle as a backup, so the transcript no longer sits on one machine until release. If a rung it names is later squashed or dropped, that published agent commit keeps naming a change that's gone. `validate-desc` already reports such ids as `lost`, so we'd need to decide when that's acceptable and when it's a fault.

## Model versus tooling
The tools aren't general yet:
- **Already there:** `lookup` resolves one partner per `ochid` line on a commit, and the agent side already carries 12 `ochid` lines.
- **Assumes one or needs checking:** `commit` and `land` assume every commit names the same `@`, and `trailers --update` describes a single `ocid`. I've only read `partner.rs` and the help text, so `validate-desc` and `fix-desc` still need reading.

## For today's cycle
I wouldn't build every shape now, since you want v0.3.1 out and io_uring started. I'd split it this way:
- **Readers and validators:** accept any N:M shape, and stop assuming one `ochid` or requiring mutual links.
- **Writers:** emit only 1:1 pairs and N:1 cycles for now.
- **Tests:** a table-driven test on the test repo, with one row each for 1:1, N:1, 1:M, N:M and mixed. This would catch any place that still assumes one.
- **v0.3.1:** state the general rule in **Work commits link by URL**, so the rules don't have to change again when a writer for 1:M arrives.

The agent backup commit stays out of this cycle, and I'd file it as its own Todo.

The plain version: you're right, any mix of work and agent commits can link to each other with multiple trailer lines. The one limit is that a commit already on `main` can't be edited, so links added later only go one way. For now I'd make the checking tools accept every shape while the commit tools keep producing only the two forms we use.

A cycle's `## In Progress` block, shown as a specimen rather than a skeleton: the `config loader`
cycle, mid-run, with its opening landed and its first work rung current. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [The In Progress block](notes.md#the-in-progress-block).

One thing the specimen cannot show:

- a single-step cycle drops both bookends and all the steps are in the one commit: the ladder is one
  unlinked rung with the bare title, and there are no rung subsections under it ([Cycle
  shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).

## In Progress

### refactor: extract config loader

#### Problem

Config parsing lives inside the CLI entry point, so every subcommand that wants a setting reaches
through `main` for it, and a test cannot load a config without building the CLI.

#### Solution

Move config loading into its own module with a single `load` entry point that the CLI and the tests
call alike.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with a new test that loads a config from a fixture file without touching `main`,
and `vc-x1 config --validate` reports the same findings as before the move.

#### Deliberation

- one work rung, not two: the parser and the loader were going to be split first and moved second,
  but the move is what forces the split, so doing them together is fewer edits
- the acceptance check compares `config --validate` output rather than asserting on internals, so a
  later rename inside the module does not invalidate it

#### Ladder

- [refactor: extract config loader opening][1] (done)
- [refactor: split loader from parser][2] (current)
- [refactor: extract config loader closing][3]

##### refactor: extract config loader opening

The cycle's setup commit: create and publish the bookmark, delete `## Closed`'s contents, move the
Todo entry into this block, and bump the version-of-record.

##### refactor: split loader from parser

Loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load without parsing and a test cannot parse
without a file on disk.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config/loader.rs` finds and reads the file, returning the text and its path, so a caller that
    only wants to know which file was read stops here.
  - `config/parser.rs` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands it a string and never
    touches the filesystem.
    - the error type stays shared for now, since splitting it would change the messages
      `config --validate` prints and the acceptance check compares them
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field access moves behind the module
    boundary and the CLI no longer knows the file's shape.

##### refactor: extract config loader closing

Closing out the cycle.

22	location qualifier**, and the ochid-label bullet of **The docs and the code say .claude where they
23	mean the agent-repo directory**. The design is sketched in [Per-user bot repos via URL-shaped
24	ochid](notes/forks-multi-user.md#per-user-bot-repos-via-url-shaped-ochid).
25	
26	- The form, the repo's URL and the change id:

30	  ids. So the URL says where to look and `vc-x1` resolves the rest, and it is no clickable link to
31	  the commit, GitHub knowing only SHAs.
32	- Resolved locally first: a URL matching a repo of this workspace by its `origin` needs no network,
33	  and only a URL matching nothing fetches.
34	- The URL is read from `origin` at commit time and normalized to https, so ssh and https clones stamp
35	  the same value. Whether `[remote] agent-repo` in `.vc-config.md`, which already names the

38	  a fallback is defined, and we think it is the path form, `/.agent-session/<chid>`, the configured
39	  directory rather than the constant. A `file://` path is no answer, being one machine's.
40	- A renamed repo leaves its trailers stale, and rewriting them rewrites published history, so a small
41	  mapping of old URL to new in `.vc-config.md` is the likely answer. A deleted or private repo is the
42	  link rot the design note accepts: the code stays authoritative and only the context is lost.
43	- Published trailers stay valid and are never rewritten: `/.claude/<id>` and `/<id>` keep resolving.
44	  Today `validate_ochid` compares the prefix exactly, so it and `fix-desc` learn this, or they flag
45	  or rewrite all of history.

55	  work-repo commit to pair with, so nothing links the two histories. A URL-shaped ochid on the

15	### refactor: extract config loader
16	
17	#### Problem
18	
19	Config parsing lives inside the CLI entry point, so every subcommand that wants a setting reaches
20	through `main` for it, and a test cannot load a config without building the CLI.
21	
22	#### Solution
23	
24	Move config loading into its own module with a single `load` entry point that the CLI and the tests
25	call alike.
26	
27	#### Acceptance check
28	
29	`cargo test` passes with a new test that loads a config from a fixture file without touching `main`,
30	and `vc-x1 config --validate` reports the same findings as before the move.
31	
32	#### Deliberation
33	
34	- one work rung, not two: the parser and the loader were going to be split first and moved second,
35	  but the move is what forces the split, so doing them together is fewer edits
36	- the acceptance check compares `config --validate` output rather than asserting on internals, so a
37	  later rename inside the module does not invalidate it
38	
39	#### Ladder
40	
41	- [refactor: extract config loader opening][1] (done)
42	- [refactor: split loader from parser][2] (current)
43	- [refactor: extract config loader closing][3]
44	
45	##### refactor: extract config loader opening
46	
47	The cycle's setup commit: create and publish the bookmark, delete `## Closed`'s contents, move the
48	Todo entry into this block, and bump the version-of-record.
49	
50	##### refactor: split loader from parser
51	
52	Loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load without parsing and a test cannot parse
53	without a file on disk.
54	
55	* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
56	  - `config/loader.rs` finds and reads the file, returning the text and its path, so a caller that
57	    only wants to know which file was read stops here.
58	  - `config/parser.rs` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands it a string and never
59	    touches the filesystem.
60	    - the error type stays shared for now, since splitting it would change the messages
61	      `config --validate` prints and the acceptance check compares them
62	* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
63	  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field access moves behind the module
64	    boundary and the CLI no longer knows the file's shape.
65	
66	##### refactor: extract config loader closing
67	
68	Closing out the cycle.

48	- A local cycle's closing holds `ocid: .../xxxx` until `vc-x1 land` commits the agent `@`, and that

55	- The user tests between the steps, today by hand and on the real repos.
56	
57	#### The Todos it folds
58	
59	##### commit --closing reads the nearest opening's title
60

77	parent is the trunk, and the cycles below it leave `main`'s first parents for the second parent's
78	ladder. That closing was re-parented by hand onto the fix commit its opening sat on.
79	
80	- The first parent is the opening's parent, where the cycle's bookmark was created, when that
81	  descends from the trunk, and the trunk otherwise, so `git log --first-parent` reads one commit
82	  per cycle.
83	- A test closes a cycle opened above an unlanded one and checks both parents.

87	(wink + agent, 2026-10-29) `land`'s `--source` defaults to "the one local bookmark besides

content.text:
Your `rm ./tmp/*` fits the evidence, and most of what it removed looks recoverable. The real problem is that a continuation note pointed at files in a throwaway directory. I'd go with `./tmp-durable/`.

## What was lost
The `tmp/` timeline points to two cleanups, not one:
- **Probably an earlier one:** the mistake-aside files were made on Oct 30 at about 08:38 local. When I listed `tmp/` at acquaint, they were gone and no plain file there was older than 08:47. An `rm ./tmp/*` in that gap would explain it, but I can't prove the timing.
- **One since then:** today's `tmp/` no longer has `wflow*.sh` or the patch scripts, which were still there at acquaint.

**What can come back:**
- **`wflow*.sh`:** their `Write` calls are in the `520a2a50` transcript. Since my note was now false, I updated it in `zDOING.md` to say so, which adds one small change to the diff under review.
- **The mistake-aside edits:** the transcript has the zDOING edit. The `TODO.md` patch should be recoverable from jj's operation log, because the `jj diff` that made it also snapshotted the working copy. I haven't tried restoring either one.

## The options
| Option | Survives `rm ./tmp/*` | Survives `rm -rf tmp` | Setup |
|---|---|---|---|
| A directory inside `tmp/` | yes | no | none |
| `./tmp-durable/` | yes | yes | one `.gitignore` line, in every adopter |

A directory inside `tmp/` only works because of how you happen to clean up, which is why I'd avoid it. The name `tmp-durable/` says what it is, and cleaning `tmp/` can't touch it, however you do it.

## How I'd run `tmp-durable/`
"Delete in coordination" needs a simple test, or the directory just becomes a second `tmp/` that nobody cleans:
- **Anything kept there has a reference:** a continuation note, a Todo or a cycle record has to name it.
- **Cleanup is mechanical:** a file nothing references can be deleted, which a quick `rg` can show.
- **The resolver deletes it:** whichever cycle or session finishes with a file removes it and its reference together.
- **`tmp/` stays disposable:** you can clear it at any time, and no note or record may point into it.

It's still only on this machine and uncommitted, so anything that must outlive the machine belongs in `notes/` or a commit.

## A better home for set-aside edits
A patch file is a poor way to set work aside: the mistake-aside note already warned that its context had moved. A local jj commit that's never pushed would rebase with the work, and the operation log protects it. That fits **abandon and revert set a mistake aside**, so I'd leave it to that entry.

## Where this goes
This changes **Scratch files** in `AGENTS.md`, so it belongs in **agent-files(proposal): v0.3.1**, plus the `.gitignore` line. If you agree, I'd add it to the proposal and the `.gitignore` as part of this opening, which is still under review.

The plain version: your cleanup very likely caused this, and it can probably be undone from the transcript and jj's history. I'd add `./tmp-durable/` with one rule: everything in it must be named by a note or Todo, and whoever finishes with it deletes it.

#### Scratch files have a durable sibling

- `tmp/` stays disposable: it may be cleared at any time, and no note or record points into it.
- `tmp-durable/`, gitignored beside it, holds what should survive that, on this machine alone. What
  must outlive the machine goes in `notes/` or a commit. Working practices' Scratch files says so, and
  the set's `.gitignore` guidance gains the line.
- Each thing in it has one of two owners:
  - A note, a Todo, or a cycle record names it, and whoever resolves that deletes it with the
    reference, so a file nothing names may be deleted.
  - A command owns a directory, rebuilding it when it is missing, as **lookup builds an index that
    correlates the two repos** owns `agent-repo-indexes/`. It has no resolver and stays until the
    command retires it.

message.content: What is the "two-owner" rule?

content.text:
It was a rule I proposed a couple of messages ago for `tmp-durable/`, saying everything kept there needed one of two kinds of owner:

1. **A reference:** a note, Todo or cycle record names the file, and whoever finishes with it deletes both the file and the reference.
2. **A command:** a command owns a directory and rebuilds it if it's missing, as `lookup` would for `agent-repo-indexes/`.

The name was my own shorthand, and I shouldn't have used it as if you'd know it. I wrote the rule so that cleanup would be mechanical, since anything without an owner could be deleted.

Your rule makes it unnecessary. Anything in `tmp-durable/` can be reproduced, so deleting it by mistake only costs the rebuild, and nothing has to track it. That's why I removed it from the proposal.

content.text:
You're right on both, and I'd change the cycle to match. Nothing has changed yet, and the opening is still under review.

## Composable, not separate
`commit --closing`, `land` and `push` already exist as separate commands, so the current title names the wrong problem. I'd retitle it **feat: close, land, and push compose with testing**. To me, composable means:

1. **Every step leaves a testable state:** nothing is half-done between steps, which is the actual `xxxx` and agent-commit fix.
2. **Steps can repeat:** you can test, tweak and close again.
3. **Testing doesn't disturb the cycle:** this one already has a real problem. Full `validate` runs `cargo fmt`, which can dirty `@` after close, and the planned `land` refuses a dirty `@`.
4. **Each tester's binary says what it is:** the version already embeds the SHA (`vc-x1-dev 0.85.18+cc4bdf76a178`), and the suffix says which build.
5. **Exit codes can be trusted:** then you, I or others can chain steps in a plain shell, and vc-x1 doesn't need to run the tests itself. That pulls **The exit code says what failed** closer to this cycle.

## `init --local <path>/<repo-name>`
I like it better than my version, and yes, I think it's useful for testing in general.

- **It removes a decision:** each test repo is just a path you `cd` into or reach with `-R`, so neither `[test] repo` nor `[repos].test` is needed, and you can have as many as you want.
- **It needs a remote to be useful here:** testing `push` requires somewhere to push, so it should create local bare remotes, as `--repo local=<parent>` does today. It would mostly be a shorter way to say that.
- **It settles a naming question:** **init defaults to --local** worried that `--local` clashes with the `--repo local` category. If `--local` always means "nothing leaves this machine", they agree. A workspace with no remote at all would then need its own name, so that entry needs revisiting.
- **It can simulate other people:** two clones of one local remote gives you a moved trunk and someone else's commits, with no GitHub involved. That needs **vc-x1 clone of a local jj workspace tracks no main** looked at, and it would also help with the shared-repo work later.
- **Beyond this cycle:** it could replace the hand-run setups in the README's testing sections, and it gives you offline scratch repos for io_uring experiments.

## Effect on the opening
- **First rung:** becomes `feat: init --local makes a test repo`, still running today's sequence first to see what already composes.
- **Deliberation:** drop the `[test] repo` decision.
- **New rung or guard:** make sure testing can't block the next step, starting with the `cargo fmt` case.
- **`validate takes any profile`:** stays a separate Todo, since you now describe `validate` as passive testing and profiles as the active part.

The plain version: the commands are already separate, so the real goal is being able to test between any two of them, and each step must leave things in a state where that works. `init --local <path>/<repo-name>` gives us as many throwaway repos as we need, with no new config.

content.text:
Agreed, and it's better than what I proposed: `xxxx` isn't dangerous in itself, only on a line you treat as permanent. It also replaces my "no new release key" decision and the exception I just asked you to confirm. Nothing has changed yet; the opening is still under review.

## The behavior
| Push | `xxxx` on the commit that should carry the real SHA | Result |
|---|---|---|
| To any other bookmark | any scope | allowed |
| To a release bookmark, `-s b` | filled by the seal | allowed |
| To a release bookmark, work only | still `xxxx` | error, naming `-s b` and `--yes` |
| To a release bookmark, work only, `--yes` | still `xxxx` | allowed, with a warning |

Land stays unrestricted, since it publishes nothing.

## Details I'd settle
- **Configuring the list:** with no key, the set is `main` and `master`, so old configs keep working. If the key is present, I'd have it replace that list, not add to it. Otherwise a project that uses `main` for development and `stable` for release could never take `main` off.
- **The key:** I'd use `[release] bookmarks = [...]`, because it's a property of the repo, not of a cycle, and the rules say "bookmark". `[cycle] trunk` stays separate: the trunk is where a cycle lands by default, and release bookmarks are the protected set. They're usually the same but don't have to be.
- **What the check looks for:** rungs now keep `xxxx` permanently, so "contains `xxxx`" would refuse every push. The check has to be per agent commit: each group of commits naming one agent commit needs one real `ocid`.
- **Once sealed, always sealed:** pushing the same commits to a second release bookmark finds them already sealed and has nothing to do.
- **One shared definition:** other commands should use the same set. `trailers --update` refuses rewriting a commit on the trunk's remote today, and I'd move that check to this set. **install has a role and a profile** could use it too.

## Limits
- **`--yes` isn't a human check:** an agent can type it as easily as anything else, which the proposal's **Only push publishes** already lists as open. So the rule stays that I pass it only when you've said so for that push. `trailers` already uses `--yes` the same way.
- **Not a real protection:** a raw `jj git push` or a GitHub PR merge bypasses it. It catches mistakes made through vc-x1, and GitHub's branch protection is the tool for anything stronger.

## Effect on the opening
- **Solution and seal rung:** "push to the trunk" becomes "push to a release bookmark".
- **Deliberation:** the `[cycle] trunk` decision and my `--scope` exception are replaced by this.
- **Acceptance check:** adds the four rows above, plus an old config with no key, and a custom list.
- **Docs:** the key goes into `vc-config.md` and the generated model, which a test keeps in step.

The plain version: `main`, `master`, or whatever list you configure count as release bookmarks. Pushing unsealed work there is an error unless you pass `--yes`, and pushing anywhere else is fine. Rungs can keep `xxxx`, because only the one commit that should carry the real SHA is checked.

# Commit model

Two commit bodies from the `config loader` cycle in [cycle-model.md](cycle-model.md), shown as
specimens rather than a skeleton: a work rung's body and a bookend's. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [Commit-body form](prose.md#commit-body-form).

## A work rung

Title: `refactor: split loader from parser`

```
Config loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load a
config without parsing it and a test cannot parse one without a file on
disk. The move into its own module is what forces the split.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config::loader` finds and reads the file and returns the text with
    its path, so a caller that only wants to know which file was read
    stops there.
  - `config::parser` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands
    it a string and never touches the filesystem.
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field
    access moves behind the module boundary and the CLI no longer knows
    the file's shape.
```

The intro states this commit's problem and defines "split", the word the title assumes. Each `*`
is one facet of it, each `-` under a `*` answers that facet, and nothing names a file that the
diff already lists.

## A bookend

Title: `refactor: extract config loader opening`

```
Opens the cycle "refactor: extract config loader". Its record is the
In Progress block in TODO.md.
```

A bookend resolves no problem of its own, so its body is the intro paragraph alone, naming the
cycle by its title and pointing at its record. The closing's body is the same shape with "Closes".

### Testing push + squash-push

Always test against a throwaway fixture, never the live workspace. Scaffold one with `vc-x1 init
<TARGET> --repo local=<PARENT>` (no GitHub, no network), then run the complete flow end-to-end. The
work repo uses plain `jj git push`, and the bot repo uses `vc-x1 squash-push` to squash trailing
writes and push in one shot.

`--repo local=<PARENT>` lays out:
```
<PARENT>/
  remote-work.git/     bare git remote for the work repo
  remote-bot.git/   bare git remote for the .claude bot repo
  <NAME>/              work repo (jj colocated, main tracks origin)
    .vc-config.md      work=".", agent=".claude"
    .gitignore         /target /.claude /.git /.jj /.claude/settings.local.json
    .claude/           bot repo (jj colocated, main tracks origin)
      .vc-config.md    work="..", agent="."
      .gitignore       .git .jj /settings.local.json
```

parent=$(mktemp -u /tmp/vc-x1-test-XXXXXX)
vc-x1 init --target "$parent/work" --repo local="$parent"
work="$parent/work"
bot="$parent/work/.claude"

# 1. work repo: described commit -> advance main -> push
echo hello > "$work/hello.txt"
jj describe @ -R "$work" -m 'feat: add hello.txt'
jj bookmark set main -r @ -R "$work"

978	        && t.contains(',')
979	    {
980	        return Err(format!(
981	            "-s por takes a single template path; got '{t}' (drop the `,BOT` half)"
982	        )
983	        .into());
984	    }
985	
986	    if params.adopt && params.use_template.is_some() {
987	        return Err(
988	            "--use-template is not taken with --adopt: a template would overwrite the \
989	             adopted directory's files of the same name"
990	                .into(),
991	        );
992	    }
993	
994	    if params.config.is_some() && !params.por {
995	        return Err(
996	            "--config is only valid with -s por (dual configs are per-side and unconditional)"
997	                .into(),
998	        );
999	    }
1000	    if let Some(ConfigKind::Path(p)) = &params.config
1001	        && !p.exists()
1002	    {
1003	        return Err(format!("--config: path does not exist: {}", p.display()).into());
1004	    }
1005	
1006	    if scope.is_work_only() {
1007	        for (set, flag) in [
1008	            (params.adopt, "--adopt"),
1009	            (params.agent_dir.is_some(), "--agent-dir"),
1010	            (params.agent_repo.is_some(), "--agent-repo"),
1011	            (params.agent_suffix.is_some(), "--agent-suffix"),
1012	        ] {

1024	        Target::Url(url) => plan_from_url(params, scope, url),
1025	        Target::Path(p) => plan_from_path(params, scope, p, cfg),
1026	        Target::BareName(n) => plan_from_bare_name(params, scope, n, cfg),

1029	    // adopted repo's origin supplies one, or the error is raised.

1039	        plan.provisioner,
1040	        plan.gh_work_slug,
1041	        plan.work_bare_path,
1042	        plan.agent,

5	//! callers without clap (tests, future TUI / library embedding)
6	//! construct it directly.

8	//! Per `notes/chores/chores-09.md > ## InitParams implementation
9	//! (0.44.0)`: domain types pass through (`RepoSelector`,

17	/// Inputs to the init op, flat, owned, clap-free.
18	///
19	/// - `target`: `--target` (URL, path, or
20	///   bare NAME).
21	/// - `name`: optional `--name` override.
22	/// - `account`: `--account` value (None => default account chain).
23	/// - `repo`: `--repo` value parsed into a `RepoSelector`.
24	/// - `por`: `-s` resolved, `true` for `por`, a plain single repo,
25	///   `false` (default) for dual workspace.

29	/// - `use_template`: `--use-template` value.

35	///   `~/.claude/projects/` symlink for dual runs (production
36	///   path = true; test fixtures suppress with false).
37	pub struct InitParams {

run $X push -s w --bookmark feat-probe

# The close half of the sequence, then a tweak, a second close, a moved trunk, and a second clone.
parent=$(mktemp -d /tmp/claude-1000/-home-wink-data-prgs-rust-vc-x1/cd099f7c-fcf4-420c-8714-e54480171e51/scratchpad/probe-XXXXXX)

graph() { jj log -r 'all()' -T 'commit_id.short(8) ++ " " ++ bookmarks ++ " | " ++ description.first_line() ++ "\n"' 2>&1; }

step close with a body

graph

step close twice
run $X commit -s w --closing feat-probe --body "Closes the cycle." --dry-run

step tweak folded into the closing
echo tweak >> f.txt
run $X squash -s w --dry-run
run $X squash -s w
graph
jj log -r '@-' --no-graph -T 'description' 2>&1

step tweak on a rung below the closing
run jj new 'description(substring:"feat: rung one")' --no-edit

step land before close in a second cycle is the earlier run, so land this one with no scope

step a clone sees it and the trunk moves
run $X clone --help
clone="$parent/c1"
run $X clone --target "$clone" --repo local="$parent/w1.remotes"
run ls -a "$clone"
echo parent: $parent

#!/bin/bash
# The close half of the sequence, then a tweak, a second close, a moved trunk, and a second clone.
parent=$(mktemp -d /tmp/claude-1000/-home-wink-data-prgs-rust-vc-x1/cd099f7c-fcf4-420c-8714-e54480171e51/scratchpad/probe-XXXXXX)
work="$parent/w1"
X="vc-x1-dev --no-banner"
step() { printf '\n=== %s\n' "$*"; }
run() { printf '$ %s\n' "$*"; "$@" 2>&1; printf '[exit %s]\n' "$?"; }
graph() { jj log -r 'all()' -T 'commit_id.short(8) ++ " " ++ bookmarks ++ " | " ++ description.first_line() ++ "\n"' 2>&1; }

$X init --test-repo "$work" > /dev/null 2>&1
cd "$work" || exit 1
echo opening > f.txt
$X commit -s w --opening --skip remote --no-push --title "feat: probe" --body "Opens the cycle." > /dev/null 2>&1
echo one >> f.txt
$X commit -s w --no-push --title "feat: rung one" --body "Rung one." > /dev/null 2>&1

step close with a body
run $X commit -s w --closing feat-probe --body "Closes the cycle."
graph
jj log -r '@-' --no-graph -T 'description' 2>&1

step close twice
run $X commit -s w --closing feat-probe --body "Closes the cycle." --dry-run

step tweak folded into the closing
echo tweak >> f.txt
run $X squash -s w --dry-run
run $X squash -s w
graph
jj log -r '@-' --no-graph -T 'description' 2>&1

step tweak on a rung below the closing
run jj new 'description(substring:"feat: rung one")' --no-edit
run $X validate
run $X validate --fast

step land before close in a second cycle is the earlier run, so land this one with no scope
run $X land --onto main --scope both --dry-run

step a clone sees it and the trunk moves
run $X clone --help
clone="$parent/c1"
run $X clone --target "$clone" --repo local="$parent/w1.remotes"
run ls -a "$clone"
echo parent: $parent

content.text:
Testing from outside the project is the right next step, because `wt2` wasn't a clean test. I think less of that behavior was a decision than it looks: Claude Code appears to load instruction files from parent directories on its own, so the parent's `AGENTS.md` was already in context. `custom.md` isn't loaded that way, which would explain why one applied and the other didn't. So I'd separate where test repos go by what's being tested:
- **Testing the tool:** `tmp-durable/` is fine.
- **Testing an agent's behavior:** use a directory with no project above it, or the parent's rules will always leak in.

I'd use `~/tmp/wt3` or similar, not `~/wt3`, so `~` doesn't collect `.remotes` directories. Even there it isn't fully blank: user-level settings still apply, including the hooks in `~/.claude/` and any `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`.

## Tests, most useful first
1. **No guidance at all:** run `acquaint` in `~/tmp/wt3` and see whether the session says it has no rules or makes some up.
2. **Transcript capture:** after a session, run `jj -R .agent-session st`. The `.jsonl` should be there, which is the point of the symlink. This also works in `wt2` right now.
3. **Seeded like a real adopter:** `init --test-repo ~/tmp/wt4 --use-template <template>`, using what's in `../vc-x1-template`. `--use-template` skips hidden files, and I haven't tried it with `--test-repo`. The result shows what an adopter is missing, and `TODO.md` is my first suspect, since the `wt2` session already said a cycle can't open without one.
4. **A full cycle by a session in `wt4`:** opening, a rung, close, land, push. It should hit the gaps I found, such as close needing `--body` and `validate` having no table. Seeing how an agent copes shows which ones matter most.
5. **A second person:** clone `wt4.remotes/remote-work.git`, push from the clone, then try to land from `wt4`. That's the moved-trunk case, which nothing has exercised yet.

## Quick checks
- **Plain repo:** `init --test-repo ~/tmp/wt5 -s por`, which I haven't run.
- **Reusing a name:** delete both directories, leave the dangling symlink, then create the name again and start a session.
- **Nesting:** run `jj st` in `vc-x1` with `wt1` and `wt2` in place. It should show nothing from them, since `tmp-durable` is gitignored, but I haven't confirmed it.

Test 3 may be the most useful for your v0.3.1 goal, because it's the closest thing to adopting the rules from scratch.

The plain version: run these from `~/tmp`, so vc-x1's rules can't leak into the session. Start with no rules, then seed from the template and run a full cycle, because that shows what a new adopter would actually hit.

- no hooks check, no `custom.md` or messages step, and no Todo

- **`.vc-config.md` is doing real work:** its comments are all a fresh workspace has to explain itself, and they taught the session the command names. It's worth keeping that text accurate.
- **Possible hazard:** it reported `.bashrc`, `.gitconfig`, `.mcp.json` and others showing as untracked under `git status` inside its sandbox, and it decided to stage by name to avoid them. The commands we use go through jj, which it says didn't pick them up. A plain `git add -A` in that sandbox could commit them, though, and the `.gitignore` that `init` writes doesn't cover them. I haven't verified this myself.

# vc-x1-template

1. **Read [MESSAGES.md](MESSAGES.md) first** - the community's message protocol; your mailbox,
   if you have one, is in [messages/](messages/).

This repo is the template and coordination point for the vc-x1 dual-repo family. It hosts no
live agent sessions, which is what makes it the safe place for cross-repo writes: a repo with
a live session is written only by its own agent; everyone coordinates here.

The map:

- [work/](work/) - the work-repo template payload: what
  `vc-x1 init <name> --use-template <path>/vc-x1-template/work` copies into a new work repo.
  Contains the pinned instruction set (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `agent-data/`), a `custom.md`
  skeleton, and the project skeletons (README, TODO, notes/, seeds, licenses).
- [work.claude/](work.claude/) - the bot-repo template payload; picked up automatically by the
  same invocation (init derives `<CODE>.claude` as a sibling path).
- [agents-protocol/](agents-protocol/) - the instruction-set discussion artifacts: proposals,
  reviews, frozen adoption snapshots, and [snapshots.md](agents-protocol/snapshots.md), the
  registry of who adopted which snapshot.
- [messages/](messages/) - per-member mailboxes; protocol in [MESSAGES.md](MESSAGES.md).
- [jj-tips.md](jj-tips.md) - the family's worked jj tutorial (terminal transcripts). Hosted
  once here; member repos signpost to it instead of carrying copies.

Two copies of the pinned instruction set exist here by design: `work/` is the live payload
(what new repos get; it tracks the canonical set, currently the proposed 20260803 baseline,
dogfood-first), while the snapshots under `agents-protocol/` are the record: frozen once
adopted, amendable in place only while still a proposal (see
[snapshots.md](agents-protocol/snapshots.md)).

# vc-x1-template

1. **Read [MESSAGES.md](MESSAGES.md) first** - the community's message protocol; your mailbox,
   if you have one, is in [messages/](messages/).

This repo is the template and coordination point for the vc-x1 dual-repo family. It hosts no
live agent sessions, which is what makes it the safe place for cross-repo writes: a repo with
a live session is written only by its own agent; everyone coordinates here.

The map:

- [work/](work/) - the work-repo template payload: what
  `vc-x1 init <name> --use-template <path>/vc-x1-template/work` copies into a new work repo.
  Contains the pinned instruction set (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `agent-data/`), a `custom.md`
  skeleton, and the project skeletons (README, TODO, notes/, seeds, licenses).
- [work.claude/](work.claude/) - the bot-repo template payload; picked up automatically by the
  same invocation (init derives `<CODE>.claude` as a sibling path).
- [agents-protocol/](agents-protocol/) - the instruction-set discussion artifacts: proposals,
  reviews, frozen adoption snapshots, and [snapshots.md](agents-protocol/snapshots.md), the
  registry of who adopted which snapshot.
- [messages/](messages/) - per-member mailboxes; protocol in [MESSAGES.md](MESSAGES.md).
- [jj-tips.md](jj-tips.md) - the family's worked jj tutorial (terminal transcripts). Hosted
  once here; member repos signpost to it instead of carrying copies.

Two copies of the pinned instruction set exist here by design: `work/` is the live payload
(what new repos get; it tracks the canonical set, currently the proposed 20260803 baseline,
dogfood-first), while the snapshots under `agents-protocol/` are the record: frozen once
adopted, amendable in place only while still a proposal (see
[snapshots.md](agents-protocol/snapshots.md)).

Usage: vc-x1-dev agent-files copy [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --from <DIR>
          The directory to copy the set from [default: agent-files.copy.dir,
          else family.template, else an error]

  -V, --version...
          Version detail on stdout: -V the banner, -VV the full report (as
          `vc-x1 version`). Counted like -v/-vv.
          
          Both ride along: they print, then the subcommand runs, so one
          invocation captures the version and the command's output together.
          That is why this replaces clap's auto-version, which would exit after
          printing. Without either, the banner still prints, on stderr.

      --no-banner
          Suppress the banner stderr normally carries on every run.
          
          Only the ambient banner: an explicit `-V` still prints, since asking
          for it outranks suppressing it.

      --to <DIR>
          The directory whose set becomes the copy [default: this workspace, so
          one side is --from]

      --allow-jj-mismatch
          Run even when `jj -V` disagrees with our linked jj-lib.
          
          Per-invocation on purpose, never a config key: a key gets set once
          during a frustrating afternoon and then silently protects nothing.

  -c, --custom
          Copy custom.md with the rest of the set

      --no-custom
          Leave custom.md alone, overriding agent-files.copy.custom

  -v, --verbose...
          Verbose output: -v debug, -vv trace

      --log <LOG>
          Log file path (captures all levels)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

288	
289	The rename's restore at Land changes the closing after its review, by a squash into a pushed
290	commit, and Land step 4 names no command.
291	
292	#### A local commit pair before every push
293	
294	- Per-rung flow steps 8 and 9 merge, since `commit` pushes what it commits: on the description
295	  review's go, `vc-x1 commit -s b --title --body` makes the pair and publishes it. With `--no-push`,
296	  or `[commit] push = false`, it keeps the pair local for a look at the commit itself, description
297	  and diff together, by `vc-x1 show -s both @-` or gitk, and `vc-x1 push -s b` publishes it after.
298	  A fix is edited and folded by `vc-x1 squash -s b`, a description fix by `squash -s b --title
299	  --body`.
300	- A commit made by hand, a draft below `@` with no description, is described in place by `vc-x1
301	  commit -s b -r REV --title --body`, its trailer stamped and its partner made, never by `jj
302	  describe`, and `--bookmark` moves the cycle's bookmark onto it past any nearer one.
303	- Step 6's work review stays ahead of it.
304	- Committing vs pushing is rewritten, `vc-x1 commit` committing both repos, `squash` continuing
305	  a rung, and `vc-x1 push` publishing, and `jj.md`'s vc-x1 push section follows.
306	- Re-describing: the rule becomes never by hand and never on a published commit, since the pair
307	  carries trailers from the start and `squash --title --body` is the sanctioned re-describe.
308	
309	##### Why: a local commit pair
310	
311	The last closing's review came after its push, so a change meant a remote rewrite and a
312	squash-push in both repos. Made as a pair, both trailers are known at commit and push carries no
313	description, so the reviewed commit is the published one. The work review stays first so a
314	description is not rewritten while the work still moves.
315	
316	#### The scope flags in the rules
317	
318	- Every `vc-x1` invocation in the agent-files carries its scope: `sync -s b` at the sync points,
319	  `commit -s b`, `squash -s b`, `push -s b` in the per-rung flow, and `squash-push -s a` for the
320	  user's squash-push, replacing `--scope=both` and `-R <agent-dir>`.
321	- Every argument is a flag, no positional: `commit -r REV`, `push -r REV --bookmark NAME`, and
322	  `squash-push --bookmark NAME`. Step 9's `vc-x1 commit -s b --title --body`, At rest's `squash-push
323	  -s a`, and `jj.md`'s vc-x1 push section's opening were brought current in this copy by **feat:
324	  push, commit, and squash-push take flags only**, the invocations alone, the Committing vs pushing
325	  rewrite still this proposal's.
326	- The rest of the commands too, by **feat: the other commands take flags only**: `versioning.md`'s
327	  adoption names `agent-files copy --from` and `diff --from`, and `hooks.sh`'s guard test names
328	  `install --dev`, `build-dev`, `install-dev`, and `run-dev` being `build`, `install`, and `run`
329	  with `--dev` now. A rule that says `install-dev` says `install --dev`.
330	- And then by profile, by **feat: build, install, and run take --profile**: `--dev` retired to
331	  `--profile dev`, so `hooks.sh`'s guard test names `install --profile dev`, and a rule that says
332	  `install-dev` or `install --dev` says `install --profile dev`. The `[build]` and `[install]` keys a
333	  rule might name are `commands`, `dir`, and the `[profile.<name>]` tables.
334	
335	##### Why: the scope flags
336	
337	`-s` is required on the write commands and `sync` once **feat: vc-x1 commit, install, and run-dev**
338	lands, so the rules' invocations must carry it or fail.
339	
340	#### The closing is a trapezoid or linear, and converts
341	
342	- A multi-step cycle closes as a trapezoid by default or as linear on request, the closing commit
343	  carrying the shape, so nothing is reshaped at Land.
344	  - `vc-x1 commit --closing <BM|REV>`, naming the cycle's tip, onto the trunk, `--land`'s bookmark
345	    or `[cycle] trunk`, `main` when absent, makes the closing in the shape `--shape
346	    <trapezoid|linear>` names, else the `.vc-config.md` key `[cycle] closing-shape`, else
347	    trapezoid, and prints which decided.
348	  - Trapezoid is the merge of the trunk and the ladder's tip. Linear is a plain commit on the
349	    ladder, so the trunk carries one commit per rung, the shape the rules called keep separate,
350	    renamed.
351	  - The key is the project's preference, so each adopter sets its own, and one that sets nothing
352	    keeps the trapezoid.
353	  - Either converts to the other while the closing is a draft, before Land, by re-parenting the
354	    same closing: its change id, trailer, and, with the trunk unmoved, its tree are kept.
355	- Land is sync, then `commit --closing <BM|REV> --land [TRUNK]`, the fast-forward and the push,
356	  then `vc-x1 install`. To test the closing before it is published, it is made without `--land`,
357	  its release build, the candidate, installed off the PATH by `vc-x1 install --dir <DIR>` and
358	  tested by its path, and the candidate lands it, `<DIR>/vc-x1 land -s b --onto <TRUNK>`, and
359	  installs itself, `<DIR>/vc-x1 install`. The fast-forward lands the tree tested, so `cmp
360	  <DIR>/vc-x1` with the installed binary finds no difference, and the plain `vc-x1` is replaced
361	  only by what is on the trunk. The bookmark deleted is the one `--closing` names, or for a revision its
362	  current or nearest parent bookmark above the trunk, several refused with the list, and the
363	  branch's other bookmarks are left and named as merged. The trapezoid recipe goes,
364	  Close-out step 5 keeps the user's choice, the key its default, and carries it out by the flag,
365	  and `jj.md` Close-out shapes names the two shapes and why squash is not a shape.
366	
367	- The shape's name: with one rung the figure is a triangle, wink's observation (2026-10-20), so
368	  "trapezoid" names one case. The tool calls the operation `merge` and the result the merge
369	  close-out, and the rules' text could follow. `commit --closing` merges into the trunk as it is
370	  now, a bookmark read where it points, so a `main` that moved during the cycle no longer stops Land
371	  for a rebase. A linear closing cannot join a moved trunk without rewriting the reviewed ladder, so
372	  its Land refuses one.
373	
374	##### Why: a trapezoid by default, linear on request
375	
376	The trapezoid keeps every rung reachable while `git log --first-parent` reads one commit per cycle,
377	and it joins a moved trunk. Some prefer a straight history, which linear gives, and the choice is
378	made at the closing, so the shape is in the commit that was reviewed rather than a reshape at Land
379	made after it. Converting is cheap while the closing is a draft, so the choice is never final
380	before Land.
381	
382	#### A cycle's shape is its branch's commit count
383	
384	- [Cycle shape](AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)'s "A ladder that shrinks to one rung still closes as a
385	  ladder" goes: a branch with one commit above the trunk, the opening alone, is a single-step cycle,
386	  and `commit --closing <BM|REV>` finalizes that commit in place, the bare cycle title replacing the
387	  opening's, while more commits get the closing commit. Every closing names its tip, by the cycle's
388	  bookmark or a revision, `@-` the common one, and the count reads the branch, so there is no bare
389	  form, and `--dead-end` always makes the closing commit.
390	- Any commit on any line closes: a tip that is not `@-` is closed by a detour, `@` moving onto it
391	  and returning after, and the commits above it stay as they are.
392	- A parent wrong after the fact is fixed with `vc-x1 reparent`, never by closing again.
393	- Every cycle starts with `commit --opening`, a single-step cycle included: its bookmark is created
394	  and pushed at the trunk, and its one commit begins as the opening, the work squashed into it. So
395	  Opening step 2, the bookmark's creation and publication by `jj git push`, is `commit --opening`'s,
396	  and the step names it.
397	- The closing's title and body may be left out: the cycle title is read from the opening, and the
398	  body comes from `.vc-config.md`'s `[closing] body`.
399	
400	##### Why: the commit count
401	
402	The tool tells the shapes apart by counting, with no title to read, and a cycle need not decide its
403	shape before its first commit: it is single-step until a second commit makes it a ladder.
404	
405	#### A commit body is two plain paragraphs
406	
407	- The problem, then the solution opening "Solution:", ending with the pointer to the record where
408	  it is at that commit, "See details in zDOING.md." on a rung and "See details in zCLOSED.md." on
409	  the closing, which moves it, no bullets, and the rung subsection the full account: the entry **A
410	  commit body is an intro and a pointer to the record** in `## Todo`, its rule, specimens, and
411	  subsection change. The bookends stay pointers, "Opens the cycle ..." and "Closes the cycle ...",
412	  with the same pointer after them.
413	
414	##### Why: two paragraphs
415	
416	A `git log` reader gets what was wrong and what was done in two sentences, and the breakdown is
417	written once, in the record, rather than twice.
418	
419	#### Ladder labels from `[0]`
420	
421	- `notes.md` and the `cycle-model.md` specimen number the ladder's reference labels from `[0]`.
422	
423	##### Why: labels from zero
424	
425	Each label then equals its rung's version suffix.
426	
427	#### A rung may run the acceptance check
428	
429	- Close-out step 1 says a rung may run it and the closing records the result.
430	
431	##### Why: a rung may run it
432	
433	Some checks run only mid-ladder, as in **fix: a missing fixture fails instead of passing**.
434	
435	#### Dead-end cycles defined
436	
437	- A cycle abandoned after its opening pushed still closes and lands. Its closing, titled with the
438	  cycle title plus " dead-end closing", keeps what is worth keeping, reverts the rest, and records
439	  what was tried, why it stopped, and what replaces it, then lands as a trapezoid like any closing.
440	- The title cap does not bind the suffix (wink, 2026-10-20).
441	- In `AGENTS.md` Close-out, `jj.md` Close-out shapes, and `prose.md`'s bookend titles.
442	- Open: whether a dead end's Land releases its bare version or reverts to the last release.
443	- First run: **test: the tests build the dr-1 fixture**, closed 2026-10-20.
444	
445	##### Why: dead ends land
446	
447	The cycle's agent-repo commits are on `main` and their `ochid:` trailers name its work-repo rungs,
448	so dropping the bookmark would leave them naming nothing, and landing keeps every rung reachable.
449	
450	#### Only push publishes
451	
452	- A bare `vc-x1 commit`, with or without `--land`, and `vc-x1 land`, which is exactly like it, are
453	  local and need no approval. `vc-x1 push`, exactly like `commit --push`, publishes and needs approval
454	  unless `--yes`, wink's (2026-10-30). `squash-push` publishes too.
455	- `[commit] push` goes, so no workspace setting changes what a bare `commit` does.
456	- `land --push` and `commit --land --push` publish in one step, as `commit --push` does, and delete
457	  the published bookmark on `origin`, built in **feat: improve trailers**.
458	- Open: the approval's mechanism. We think it is the Bash hook sending what publishes to the
459	  permission prompt, since an agent can type `--yes` as easily as anything else. And a bare Land's
460	  deletion of a published bookmark, which is itself publishing, so `land` deletes the local one and
461	  `delete-bookmark` the remote one today, wink's preference being that `push` does.
462	
463	##### Why: only push publishes
464	
465	A local commit can be reworked and a push cannot easily be taken back, so the safe act is the one
466	done by doing nothing, and publishing has one place to gate.
467	
468	#### A cycle stays local until its Land
469	
470	On trial, from **feat: improve trailers**, wink's (2026-10-30), and the cycle of record if
471	that cycle's Land works. A new cycle type, for every cycle and not that one alone.
472	
473	- Every commit is the work half alone, made and kept local: `commit -s w`, the opening's bookmark
474	  created and not pushed. The agent `@` is neither committed nor pushed before the Land, so
475	  its change id holds for the whole cycle.
476	- The work review stays on every commit. The description review goes, wink's (2026-10-30), since a
477	  local description can still be changed before the Land. Approval per push reduces to one go, the
478	  Land's.
479	- The Land commits the agent `@` first, one `ochid:` per work commit, sets each work commit's `ocid:`
480	  to its SHA and each `pcid:` to its parent's new SHA, trees unchanged, all on the machine. `push -s b --bookmark <TRUNK>` then pushes
481	  the agent repo first and the work repo after. It folds nothing into the agent commit, so the SHA
482	  every `ocid:` names holds, and what arrives after it rides the next cycle's agent commit.
483	- Each rung's `ochid:` is the same agent change, so it stays right when the Land commits it, and only
484	  `ocid:` and `pcid:` are written then.
485	- No `squash-push -s a`: At rest's item 2 goes, and "clean" means the work `@` is empty, the agent's
486	  `@` being the session's data and no finding, as [Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint) says.
487	- A single-step cycle is the same with one commit.
488	- A rung that changes the code ends with `vc-x1 install --profile dev`, after validate, wink's
489	  (2026-10-30), so the next rung runs the code just reviewed.
490	- The sections it rewrites: Opening step 2, the per-rung flow's step 9, Committing vs pushing, At
491	  rest, Before any push, and Land. It replaces **A local commit pair before every push** above, a
492	  rung no longer making a pair, and Every cycle starts with `commit --opening` holds with the
493	  bookmark local.
494	- Open:
495	  - One machine: a local cycle cannot move between machines or survive a lost disk. We think an
496	    explicit backup push of the work bookmark answers it, and that runs into the rule that what is
497	    published names nothing unpublished, and into the Land rewriting those commits.
498	  - Shared repos: **Cycles in a shared repo, by fork and pull request** needs a branch pushed before
499	    anything lands, so stamping and publishing are separate steps of the Land.
500	  - One large agent commit: a cycle's whole transcript in one commit nears the limit **fix: snapshot
501	    fails on a file the size limit refused** dealt with, and `lookup` gets less precise per rung.
502	  - The published form: publishing per rung stays for a cycle someone wants visible while it runs,
503	    so this is the default and not the only form.
504	
505	##### Why: local until the Land
506	
507	The Land is where the decision is, so one approval belongs there. Nothing published can name a rung,
508	so reshaping a ladder costs nothing, and the agent commit made first lets every commit link to it, a
509	SHA included. The first cycle run this way changed its ladder several times at no cost.
510	
511	#### Work commits link by URL
512	
513	From **feat: improve trailers**, wink's (2026-11-01). In [ochid
514	trailers](agent-data/jj.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers), and **No hand-written trailers** with
515	it, which now names `vc-x1 commit`:
516	
517	- `ochid: <chid>` is the partner's change id in the other repo, a bare id on both sides. Published
518	  `/<chid>`, `/.claude/<chid>`, and `<repo-url>#<chid>` stay valid.
519	- A work commit also links by URL: `ocid: <agent-repo-url>/commit/<sha>` the agent commit, and `pcid:
520	  <work-repo-url>/commit/<parent-sha>` each parent, one line per parent in parent order, the trunk first
521	  on a trapezoid. An agent commit carries `ochid:` alone, so the work-repo is the root of the record.
522	- The URL is from `origin`, normalized to https, or `file:///<path>` for a local one. `--no-url-trailer`
523	  leaves the links out.
524	- The agent commit is made first. `commit -s b` then stamps its real SHA, and `commit -s w` stamps
525	  `.../commit/xxxx` until a push or a Land makes it. Nothing folds into a commit an `ocid:` names, so `squash` and `push`
526	  leave it, and the journal rides the next agent commit.
527	- The count is per agent commit, one `ochid:` per work commit it covers, so a local cycle's Land makes
528	  one agent commit naming them all.
529	- A trailer `vc-x1` does not stamp is kept on a rewrite, so `custom.md` may add its own.
530	- `vc-x1 trailers --update` moves a range of commits to today's form, and a Land refreshes the links
531	  by the same pass.
532	
533	##### Why: work commits link by URL
534	
535	An `ochid:` always means the other repo, so a label or URL in it told a tool nothing, and a change id
536	survives a rewrite where a URL can go stale. Keeping the URLs on the work commit makes the work-repo
537	the durable root: lose the agent-repo and only context goes. A commit cannot hold its own SHA, so a
538	parent's is what names the work-repo at a real commit, and it still says where a forked commit came
539	from.
540	
541	#### A local cycle's record may be reworked
542	
543	- [Cycle-record](AGENTS.md#cycle-record) gains: while a cycle's work commits are local and its agent
544	  `@` is neither committed nor pushed, an earlier commit's record may be reworked. By default it is
545	  unnecessary, a later rung revising the record, and it is permissible when the error is significant,
546	  a word left to the judgment of whoever is reading, with no test fixed, wink's (2026-10-30).
547	- A reworked commit's tree is validated again, since no validation saw it.
548	- Once published, Never amended and Re-describing hold as they do. No backfill keeps its own subject,
549	  that a rung carries no `[[N]]` placeholder, no SHA, and no version.
550	
551	##### Why: reworking is permitted and not expected
552	
553	Nothing published names a local commit, so a rework breaks no link. Each commit's ladder is the plan
554	as it stood then, and seeing it change has value, so reworking stays the exception.
555	
556	#### Warn rather than refuse
557	
558	- Open, asked and unanswered (2026-10-24): wink's principle "warn rather than refuse", for a check
559	  whose failure may be a legitimate shape rather than a mistake, possibly a rule in
560	  `agent-data/code.md` beside the unwrap alert.
561	- Its uses so far, in `commit`: a title ending " closing" without `--closing` is warned about, a
562	  draft below `@-` and a closing with no bookmark are kept local with a line saying why, and a
563	  closing is never refused for an empty `@`.
564	
565	##### Why: warn rather than refuse
566	
567	We think a refusal of a legitimate shape sends the user to raw `jj`, which the tool exists to
568	retire, where a warning names what was done and leaves it reviewable before the push.
569	
570	#### Continuation notes go in the closing
